newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadians protest Wal-Mart's Cuban product removal.
newsitem.headline: Canadians protest Wal-Mart's Cuban product removal.

text.p: Singing "O Canada" and waving the flag, a group of about 30 Winnipeg citizens took a stand at the Grant Park Wal-Mart Sunday, according to a report from the Canadian Press news agency.
The Manitoba-Cuba Solidarity Committee held informational picketing to criticize the U.S.-based chain's decision to pull Cuban-made pajamas from the shelves of its Canadian stores.
"It's beyond legality," said Fagie Fainman, co-chairwoman of the committee. "It's immoral."
The American retail giant pulled the pajamas in conformity with the U.S. Helms-Burton Act, which penalizes countries and companies that do business with Cuba.

"They're adhering to American law, not Canadian policy, which says we are to trade with the world," said Fainman. "Consumers have a right to decide what we're going to buy. Either put the pajamas back on the shelves or pack up and go back to America."
